```{r}
library(glmseg)
set.seed(1)
n <- 600
y <- c(rnorm(200, 0, 1), rnorm(200, 8, 1), rnorm(200, -6, 1))

# Fixed K = 3
fit <- glmseg(y, K = 3, family = gaussian_homo(), init = "binseg")
fit
summary(fit)

# Automatic selection of K by BIC
sel <- select_k(y, K_max = 5, family = gaussian_homo(), init = "binseg")
sel$K
sel$bic

# Comparison with GFPOP (mean model)
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("gfpop", quietly = TRUE)}
gfpop_gauss(y, K = 3)$bp
```

## Non-Gaussian families

`glmseg` supports logistic and Poisson losses through the same interface.

```{r}
set.seed(3)
n <- 600
yb <- c(rbinom(300, 1, plogis(-1.6)), rbinom(300, 1, plogis(1.6)))
glmseg(yb, K = 2, family = logistic_family(), init = "binseg")$bp

yc <- c(rpois(300, exp(0.4)), rpois(300, exp(2.2)))
glmseg(yc, K = 2, family = poisson_family(), init = "binseg")$bp
```

## Survival (Weibull-AFT) segmentation

For right-censored data, `survseg()` detects change-points in a Weibull-AFT model
(requires the `survival` package).

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)}
set.seed(5)
n <- 600
X <- matrix(1, n, 1)
tt <- c(rweibull(300, shape = 1.3, scale = exp(0.3)),
        rweibull(300, shape = 1.3, scale = exp(3.0)))
cc <- rexp(n, rate = 1 / 80)
time <- pmin(tt, cc); status <- as.numeric(tt <= cc)
survseg(time, status, K = 2, init = "binseg")$bp
```
